react_result.final_narrative_text: Four complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: disruption of tryptophan metabolism. In the RaMP multi-database ORA, KEGG:map00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' is the top hit (FDR 1.5e-14, fold-enrichment 667), with six of nine input metabolites mapped (L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, quinolinic acid, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid). The MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA confirms KEGG:hsa00380 at p=1.03e-06, and Mummichog's m/z-direct network analysis independently recovers 'Tryptophan metabolism' as its top-ranked pathway (p=0.00193). L-Leucine and 3-sulfinoalanine contribute as secondary hits in the valine/leucine/isoleucine and cysteine/methionine branches respectively. The six driver metabolites span three functional segments of the tryptophan catabolic network: the serotonin/melatonin branch (tryptamine, serotonin, melatonin, L-tryptophan), the kynurenine/quinolinic acid branch (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, quinolinic acid), and the polyamine branch (putrescine via the urea-cycle overlap). Cross-paradigm evidence is strong — the same pathway dominates ORA-based, mass-feature-based, and KEGG-hierarchical perspectives simultaneously. The biological story is consistent with immune activation driving tryptophan depletion via the IDO pathway (reflected in WP:WP5414, FDR 1.4e-08), shunting flux toward the kynurenine branch and accumulating quinolinic acid and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, while simultaneously reducing serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis. This pattern is a hallmark of inflammation, interferon-gamma activation, and the tryptophan–kynurenine–NAD+ axis disrupted in neuroinflammatory and mood disorders.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant signal in this nine-metabolite differential set. RaMP ORA identifies KEGG:map00380 "Tryptophan metabolism" as the top hit with FDR 1.5e-14, supported by six mapped metabolites including L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, quinolinic acid, and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA confirms the same pathway (KEGG:hsa00380) at p-value 1.03e-06. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently ranks "Tryptophan metabolism" first with p-value 0.0012, providing orthogonal mass-spectrometry evidence. Within this dominant signal, two sub-branches are active: the serotonin/melatonin arm (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR 3.47e-08) and the kynurenine/NAD+ arm (WP:WP4210, FDR 1.10e-10). The IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR 1.4e-08) connects the two, reflecting the known immune-driven shunt of tryptophan flux. Driver metabolites L-tryptophan (C00078), serotonin (C00780), melatonin (C01598), and quinolinic acid (C03722) are all confirmed members of these pathways. Secondary branch hits include L-leucine in valine/leucine/isoleucine biosynthesis (KEGG:hsa00290) and putrescine in urea cycle/amino group metabolism (MUMM:urea_cycle_amino_group_metabolism), while 3-sulfinoalanine maps to cysteine/methionine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00430).

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant signal in this nine-metabolite differential set. RaMP ORA identifies KEGG:map00380 "Tryptophan metabolism" as the top hit with FDR 1.5e-14, supported by six mapped metabolites including L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, quinolinic acid, and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA confirms the same pathway (KEGG:hsa00380) at p-value 1.03e-06. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently ranks "Tryptophan metabolism" first with p-value 0.0012, providing orthogonal mass-spectrometry evidence. Within this dominant signal, two sub-branches are active: the serotonin/melatonin arm (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR 3.47e-08) and the kynurenine/NAD+ arm (WP:WP4210, FDR 1.10e-10). The IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR 1.4e-08) connects the two, reflecting the known immune-driven shunt of tryptophan flux. Driver metabolites L-tryptophan (C00078), serotonin (C00780), melatonin (C01598), and quinolinic acid (C03722) are all confirmed members of these pathways. Secondary branch hits include L-leucine in valine/leucine/isoleucine biosynthesis (KEGG:hsa00290) and putrescine in urea cycle/amino group metabolism (MUMM:urea_cycle_amino_group_metabolism), while 3-sulfinoalanine maps to cysteine/methionine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00430).
